security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG decoder for PLI.DB/PLI.DH/PLUI.DH (RV32 register-pair variants) fails to enforce the 'if (rd_p != 0)' guard when rd_p=0, causing writes to x0 (breaking the architectural zero-register invariant) and to x1 (corrupting the return-address register), or the 4-bit rd_p field is incorrectly decoded causing writes to wrong register pairs
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: rd_p == 0 check missing OR rd_p field width != 4 bits OR XLEN gate missing for RV64-only PLI.W/PLUI.W OR non-contiguous immediate bit extraction (imm[8:0|9], imm[6|15:7], imm[22|31:23])
security_spec.summary: P-ext Load Immediate instructions use OP-IMM-32 encoding with non-standard split immediate fields and RV32 register-pair destinations guarded by rd_p!=0 checks — TCG decode errors can corrupt x0/x1 register invariants or load wrong immediates

findings.finding: No PLI/PLUI decode entries exist. All 8 instructions (PLI.B, PLI.H, PLI.W, PLUI.H, PLUI.W, PLI.DB, PLI.DH, PLUI.DH) are absent from the decode table. The RISC-V P-ext spec (src/unpriv/zp.adoc) is explicitly a placeholder awaiting ratification — no normative instruction definitions exist to implement against.

findings.finding: gen_set_gpri() correctly sign-extends on RV32 via (int32_t) cast. No PLI-specific translator calls this function — the spec hasn't defined PLI.B/PLI.H/PLI.W/PLUI.H/PLUI.W instructions.

gen_set_gpr_pair() demonstrates the register-pair write pattern with odd-register rejection. No PLI.DB/PLI.DH/PLUI.DH translator calls these functions — no such instructions are defined in the current spec.
